title: Ali al-Zaidi Named Prime Minister-Designate; Youngest PM in Modern Iraq
detail: Iraqi President Nizar Amedi (PUK-Kurdish) formally named Ali Faleh al-Zaidi as prime minister-designate on April 27, 2026. Al-Zaidi, a 39-year-old businessman from Dhi Qar Province with no prior political office, is potentially the youngest prime minister in Iraq's modern history. His nomination was advanced by the Coordination Framework (Shi'a bloc) and received signals of US approval. Al-Zaidi's designation followed a protracted government-formation crisis after the October 2025 elections. He was given 30 days to form a cabinet and seek a parliamentary confidence vote. His selection by Iran-aligned forces while also securing US backing reflects the balancing act Iraq has maintained throughout the post-ISIS era.

media.caption: Ali al-Zaidi named PM-designate — 39-year-old businessman from Dhi Qar, potentially youngest PM in modern Iraqi history

title: Kurdistan Region Reports 809 Drone and Missile Attacks in 50 Days Amid Iran-Iraq War Spillover
detail: The Kurdistan Regional Government announced on April 27, 2026 that the Kurdistan Region had been struck by 809 drone and missile attacks in the 50-day period from February 28 to April 20, 2026. The barrage resulted in 20 deaths and 123 injuries. Iran-aligned Iraqi proxy militias (PMF factions including Kata'ib Hezbollah and Harakat al-Nujaba) and direct Iranian launches were identified as the primary actors, targeting KRG territory in the context of the broader regional conflict following the US-Iran war. The cumulative attack total highlighted the disproportionate impact on Kurdistan — a US partner region — of a conflict nominally between the US and Iran.

media.caption: Kurdistan Region reports 809 drone and missile attacks in 50 days — 20 killed, 123 wounded — Iran-aligned PMF factions responsible
